claims.claim: The tuples a=(2,3,5,12) and b=(1,1,1,4,6,9) satisfy the positive-integer hypotheses, and their Landau function is 1-periodic.
claims.evidence: Both tuples are nonempty and all entries are positive integers. Their sums equal 22. For every real x, floor(n(x+1))=floor(nx)+n, so L(x+1)-L(x)=22-22=0.
claims.search_method: Exact integer validation and the integer-shift identity for floors.

claims.claim: These tuples satisfy L(x)≥0 for every real x≥0.
claims.evidence: The checker constructs every numerator and denominator breakpoint, partitioning [0,1) into 22 half-open intervals. On each [u,v), for every tuple entry n, it verifies m<=n*u and n*v<=m+1 with m=floor(n*u). These inequalities prove floor(nx)=m for every real x in the interval. Every resulting Landau value is nonnegative. Periodicity extends this certificate to all real x>=0. The draft's entire denominator-breakpoint table also matches.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive rational breakpoint construction with exact inequalities certifying constancy throughout every interval; no sampling inference.

claims.claim: The corresponding q-factorial ratio is D(q)=[10]_q[11]_q(1-q²+q⁴), a polynomial in Z[q] of degree 23.
claims.evidence: Independently multiplying the original q-factorials gives numerator N of degree 80 and denominator B of degree 57. Exact polynomial division has zero remainder and quotient [10]_q[11]_q(1-q²+q⁴). Independent cross multiplication verifies B times this polynomial equals N coefficient by coefficient. The quotient has integer coefficients and degree 9+10+4=23.
claims.search_method: Arbitrary-precision integer polynomial multiplication, exact long division, and cross multiplication from the original factorial definitions.

claims.evidence: Multiplication of the independently obtained exact quotient by 1+q reproduces all 25 displayed coefficients. Its leading coefficient is 1 at degree 24, so the sequence is complete. The draft's coefficient formula independently agrees at every index.
claims.witness: (1+q)[10]_q[11]_q(1-q²+q⁴) expands to exactly the displayed sequence; its coefficient sum is 220.
claims.search_method: Exact integer convolution and coefficient-by-coefficient comparison, including degree and coefficient-formula checks.

claims.claim: The displayed coefficient sequence is not unimodal, providing a complete refutation of the recorded conjecture.
claims.evidence: If a unimodal peak h>=12 existed, its nondecreasing prefix would require c_10<=c_12, contradicting 16>14. If h<12, its nonincreasing suffix would require c_12>=c_14, contradicting 14<16. The checker additionally rejects all 25 possible peak indices. Since the tuples satisfy every recorded hypothesis, this is a complete counterexample.
claims.search_method: Complete logical case split on the peak index and exhaustive exact checking of the defining inequalities.
